{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the clock is running. I'll claim the pad and sketch a fish with a tail fin, since a fish outline reads clearly to a judge. Then the table can start building it.",
  "say": "Okay, I'm grabbing the pad. Let's do a fish: a clear outline with a forked tail fin is easy to recognise when it falls. I'll sketch it now, and then we can trace it in pieces.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 6], [9, 8.5], [14, 8.5], [19, 9], [22, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[22, 10], [19, 11], [14, 11.5], [9, 11.5], [4, 14]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 6], [6, 10], [4, 14]]},
    {"type": "circle", "cx": 18, "cy": 9.5, "r": 0.6},
    {"type": "label", "x": 3, "y": 10, "text": "START"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish facing right. START at top of tail fin (4,6). Stroke 1: top edge of body to nose (22,10). Stroke 2: bottom edge back to tail bottom (4,14). Stroke 3: fork of tail fin from start down to notch and bottom (6,10). Eye circle at (18,9.5). Need someone on stroke 1 first, since it leaves START. Check the pad sketch before tracing."
